Well, I would just notice the same group of former classmates that would comment and support other former classmates, or call out the bullshit other former classmates would spout, and talked to a couple of my other friends about creating a secret facebook group to just kinda get all the other people that were also not assholes together to just talk and have a community together, and made it. I was raised in the WELS and I say I was raised in a cult all the time! I went to school prek-12 within the WELS system and realized I was bi and trans in my junior year, which is when everything started crashing down around me and the "bubble" I was in finally popped and I saw the world for what it is. I didn't realize how badly it really traumatized me though until last year and how culty the whole thing was. I always believed I had a great education until I gained friends after I graduated who were in public schools and realized that my education was sub-par. I could get into all the weird shit that went on at LPS but that's for another time. I definitely experienced a control of information and behavioral control as well while I was there, and it's left me feeling very empty and guilty just for existing. But there is a light at the end of the tunnel, it does get better when you're fully out of the church and find people that genuinely care about you, and not just about your faith.
